comment: Ownership map for the private Cloud overlay (backenly/backenly-cloud).
PUBLIC IS THE DEFAULT. A path listed here is one the private overlay is
ALLOWED to own; everything not listed belongs to the public product and the
overlay may never write it. Enforced by scripts/verify-overlay-boundary.ts.
Ownership is whole-directory wherever a private subsystem can have a
directory of its own, so the overlay only ever ADDS files and never has to
overwrite one the public repository tracks. Two paths are deliberate
file-level exceptions, both because their directory is MIXED and claiming
the whole of it would take public product code with it:
prisma/seed-billing.ts                  billing seed data, no directory
app/api/projects/[id]/access/route.ts   team management under a route
family that is otherwise entirely
per-project product
Phases 6 and 7 performed the removals. Phase 7 emptied the transition list:
no public file remains under a private-owned path.
Phase 4 grandfather list: public files that already lived under a path the
overlay would eventually own. It was legal only until Phases 6 and 7 moved
them, and it could SHRINK but never grow.
It is now EMPTY. Phase 6 took it from 73 to 14, and Phase 7 moved the
remaining 14 -- the organization routes, lib/org, OrgSwitcher and the fleet
scripts -- so nothing is grandfathered any more.
The key is kept rather than deleted because deleting it is the same commit
that moves CI to --strict, and that is Phase 8 work with its own acceptance.
An empty list is already strictly enforced: the verifier fails on any NEW
public file under a private-owned path, and its stale-entry check means an
entry cannot be re-added for a file that is not actually there.
